subject: Immediate exec attention: ClearCore reserved-capacity deficit & GPU pool choke
messages:
From: Alex Billings <alex.billings@clearcore.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: support@clearcore.com
Date: 2028-02-12T15:12:00Z
Subject: Sudden latency & 5xx surge — reserved throughput under-delivering

Naomi —

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latencies at ~14:40 PST and a corresponding rise in 5xx errors from your dedicated pool. Throughput has dropped ~32% vs our SLA baseline (measured by requests/min to the reserved endpoint). This is impacting ClearCore Checkout for US-region traffic — cart failures are up and our fraud-scoring pipeline is lagging.

Attached are the production graphs (latency percentiles, error rate, queue depth) and a short CSV with request ids that hit 500s. Our ops team has ruled out app-layer regressions on our side.

We need:
- Immediate mitigation plan (burst, fallback, or alternate model routing).
- Exec-level commitment on capacity/credits if this is a platform-side saturation.
- An ETA for restored baseline throughput and remediation steps we can share with merchant ops.

We are preparing a postmortem but need a short bridge plan now — can your team authorize emergency burst capacity and toggle any noisy-tenant protections?

Alex
Alex Billings
Head of Engineering, ClearCore
alex.billings@clearcore.com
Attachment: prod-graphs-20280212.png (image/png, 1.2MB stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Billings <alex.billings@clearcore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-12T15:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx surge — reserved throughput under-delivering

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. We see the same signals in our telemetry (queue length spike + KV cache churn) for the GPU pool serving ClearCore's reserved capacity. I'm looping in the ops and sales leads to coordinate an immediate bridge.

Short immediate plan (what we can do in the next 15–60 minutes):
- Authorize a temporary burst from Dedicated → Dedicated burst pool for 4 hours (manual authorization).
- Enable targeted prefix-caching for your highest-volume routes to reduce token compute for repeated calls.
- Apply noisy-tenant throttles if unrelated tenants are saturating the pool.
- Open a dedicated Zoom; Marissa, can you spin up the incident bridge?

We will need an exec decision on the following before we commit to any customer credit or extended burst:
- Burst budget (tokens / GPU hours) we approve immediately.
- Credit offer to offset impacted usage if this is a Redwood capacity issue.

I will follow up on the bridge with the MAP-draft attached (proposed mutual action plan).

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Attachment: MAP-draft-ClearCore.pdf (application/pdf, 560KB stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-12T15:37:00Z
Subject: Internal: decision needed — ClearCore emergency burst & credit guidance

Team —

Summary: ClearCore (D-4472) is experiencing dedicated pool saturation in us-west and reserved-capacity throughput has dropped ~32% vs baseline. Customer-facing impact: cart failures and delayed fraud scoring. Customer wants emergency burst + clarity on credits.

Decision points (need an answer in 30m):
1) Approve temporary burst: up to 250k tokens/min sustained for 4 hours (est. cost $X, see attached burst-approval-sheet.csv).
2) Credit: offer 10% usage credit for the incident window vs ClearCore's last invoice? 15% if we take full ownership (ops root cause).
3) Ops mitigations: authorize noisy-tenant isolation and model fallback to 1 smaller quantized variant for non-critical routes.

Operational asks (Marissa / Ops): can you confirm whether noisy-tenants are present and whether prefix caching can be toggled without schema changes?

Vivek — if we take the credit at 15% we need exec signoff; please advise whether you want me to escalate to the CEO/Finance for final approval or we can approve from leadership.

Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-12T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: decision needed — ClearCore emergency burst & credit guidance

Naomi — thanks. I reviewed the telemetry and did a quick cost delta. Recommend the following so we can move fast:

- Approve the 4-hour temporary burst capped at the numbers Naomi proposed (250k tokens/min sustained cap). Ops should gate after 4 hours and report back.
- Approve a provisional 10% credit against the impacted billing window; escalate to 15% only if post-incident RCA shows Redwood capacity/serving regression.
- In parallel, Ops: identify and throttle any noisy tenants contributing >15% of pool load. If identified, initiate cross-tenant mitigation and notify those customers.

I will authorize up to $Y in slack burst spend for this bridge; Marissa please coordinate and confirm when the burst is active.

Marcus Lin
VP, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Billings <alex.billings@clearcore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, support@clearcore.com
Date: 2028-02-12T19:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx surge — reserved throughput under-delivering

Alex — quick status update and actions we've taken on your behalf: 

- We authorized a four-hour emergency burst starting 19:25 UTC (confirmed by Ops). You should see throughput return toward baseline within 10–15m as queued work drains; we also enabled targeted prefix-caching for your high-volume routes.
- We provisionally applied a 10% usage credit for the impacted window; we will finalize the exact credit after the post-incident RCA.
- Ops identified one noisy tenant on the same GPU pool and applied throttles — we will follow up with affected teams.

Next steps:
1) Bridge is open — Marissa (ops) is running the incident room and will share real-time metrics.
2) Post-incident RCA and corrective actions within 72 hours.
3) If the RCA shows Redwood serving regressions, we will escalate credit to 15% and produce a remediation timeline.

Suggested sync: 10:00 PST tomorrow to review RCA draft and confirm any contractual remediation. Please reply if that works for you.

Thanks for flagging this quickly — we’ll keep the bridge running until you confirm normal behavior.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Attachment: burst-approval-sheet.csv (text/csv, 2KB stub)
